matching.note: Before comparing: trim spaces at the start and end, and turn repeated spaces into one. Upper and lower case matter, because Git cares about them too.

boxStates.empty: A plain wooden box locked by a hiding spell. Git can't see it.
boxStates.initialized: The spell is broken: the lid is open and a .git sticker glows on the box.

stations.title: The Workshop
stations.story: The cat arrives at its workshop, a bit lost. Its brand-new software is hidden inside a plain wooden box by a hiding spell, so Git can't see it.

cat.intro: Hey code traveler! I'm a bit lost... and someone used magic to hide my new software in this box!
cat.task: Can you cast the spell that lets Git see inside it?
cat.hint: Psst... every Git spell starts with git. The second word is short for "initialize", and it's only 4 letters!
cat.success: WOW, you have real magical powers! The spell is broken: a hidden .git folder appeared, so Git can see my software and remember every change now. I wanna be friends with you ^_^
cat.failure: Hmm... the box didn't even blink. That's not the right spell. Start with git, then the word that sets it up!

commonMistakes.feedback: Sooo close! Your spell is missing one tiny letter in the second word.
Right idea, but Git likes its spells short! Try the 4-letter version.
Every Git spell needs its magic word first: git!
Careful, traveler! Spells are case-sensitive. Write git in small letters.
There's no start spell in Git's spellbook... think of a word that means "set up".
